stop_condition: Stop when R4-F1 is adjudicated closed or still-open with a concrete failure path, the single-parse property is confirmed or refuted, and the 13-read residual is judged. Scope is review-check.sh only.

findings.evidence: R4-F1's separate post-validation reread is closed: lines 1185-1241 project task_id, unit_ids, and unit_content only from vout; line 1002 derives unit_content from the same in-memory block, and its recursive key sorting plus tojson is byte-equivalent to the legacy jq -cS representation. The disclosed residual at lines 755, 767-798, and 813 is nevertheless fail-open. Let valid artifact A pass the eight heading greps and sentinel count/line reads; after line 798, atomically replace it with B, which omits the required headings and sentinels but places a fully schema-valid JSON object carrying A's task_id and U1 between A's recorded line numbers. awk at line 813 captures B, every later check validates that in-memory object, and validate-design emits ok:true. Restoring A immediately after awk also leaves authentic on-disk A and its hash alongside B-derived unit_content, without triggering any guard.
findings.description: The design-unit-json second extraction is gone, but validate-design still does not validate one file snapshot. Its 13-read residual can combine structural checks from A with unit content from B and return success, so the residual is not fail-closed. Consumers can consequently bind or clear using unit bytes that did not come from the artifact whose structure and external hash they trust.
